newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total to invest in Middle East.
newsitem.headline: Total to invest in Middle East.

text.p: French oil group Total SA said on Tuesday that after years of focussing expansion outside the Middle East, mainly in Asia, the group would now relaunch expansion in the "key oil region for the 21st century".
Christophe de Margerie, director for the Middle East, said the group would make important investments in 1997 and 1998 in the region in new reserves and exploration projects.
"The investments in 1996 will be significantly higher than in 1995, the same for 1997 and 1998. For a start they will be double than the 600 million francs of 1995," he told a news conference.

"We do not refrain ourselves from working with whatever country in the region. We are in Iran and we hope to be in Iraq. Politics is not really our business. The countries in the Middle East will develop and we have to be there," he said, adding investments had already been made in Qatar, Oman and will be made soon in Yemen.
Christophe de Margerie said that a contract for technical assistance with Kuwait could soon be signed.
"It's not the technical assistance that interests us but we could do it in a first phase when there is a chance that exploration may be open to oil companies," he said.

The Middle East, where Total has been active for more than 70 years since its pumped its first oil in former Persia, contributed 700 million francs to the 1995 operating profit, or some nine percent of the total.
